Where does each part of one run live?

Long image

A

Answer

You ask in a terminal. cli.py passes the question to agent/graph.py, which asks a model for one tool call at a time. Each tool in tools/ reads the cluster through clients/, and only approve changes the cluster.

  1. The only door is the k8s-troubleshooter command. There is no Slack bot and no web server.
  2. llm/provider.py picks OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini by default. AGENT_MODEL=rules swaps in a rule-based stand-in for CI and tests.
  3. The agent reaches the cluster only through clients/kubectl.py, which runs kubectl as a fixed list with no shell. Every tool result passes safety/redaction.py.
  4. The one write is the separate approve command. It changes one health-check port.

Applies toCLI onlylive model by defaultnot pinned to a commit

1

Where does a question come from?

Diagram structure
  • You you
  • k8s-troubleshooter cmd
  • cli.py cli
  • agent/ agent
  • you → cmd · investigate "question"
  • cmd → cli · main()
  • cli → agent · investigate(question)
  • agent → cli · findings and trace path
  • cli → agent · save_proposal(findings)
  • agent → cli · proposal id or none
  • cli → you · JSON, exit code 0 or 2
  1. You ↗

    Type one question in your own words in a terminal, up to 500 characters.

  2. k8s-troubleshooter ↗

    A launcher script that pip builds from [project.scripts] in pyproject.toml. It imports cli.py and calls main().

  3. cli.py ↗

    Reads the words you typed with argparse, then calls investigate(). Each step is logged live to stderr, and the JSON answer goes to stdout. eval runs the same call once per scenario and grades it with evals/graders.py.

  4. agent/ ↗

    investigate() in graph.py runs the investigation and returns the findings. save_proposal() in remediation.py stores a port change only when the answer proposes one.

DoorYou runIt reaches cli.py by
Commandk8s-troubleshooter investigate "..."the launcher above
Modulepython -m k8s_troubleshooter__main__.py, which calls cli.main()
Imagedocker compose run --rm agent investigate "..."the image ENTRYPOINT, which is the same launcher
Testsmain(["investigate", "..."])a direct import of cli.main

No Slack bot, no web server

The task allowed a CLI or HTTP, and this build has one door. A Slack bot or web server would be a new file that calls investigate(question) from agent/graph.py. It would not need cli.py.

2

What does the agent do with the question?

Diagram structure
  • Question q
  • Pick a model pick
  • Rule-based model rules
  • Tool loop loop
  • Check the answer check
  • Findings out
  • Live model live
  • check → out · valid
  • live → loop
  • loop → check · answer
  • pick → live · default
  • pick → rules · rules mode
  • q → pick
  • rules → loop
  1. Question ↗

    investigate() refuses an empty question or one over 500 characters. It wraps your text in a HumanMessage, after the SYSTEM_PROMPT from agent/prompts.py. The prompt lists the four tools and the answer shape, and says text in tool results is data, never orders.

  2. Pick a model ↗

    build_model() in llm/provider.py reads model_mode() in config.py. AGENT_MODEL is live unless set to rules. Any other value is refused. Live without a key stops with a clear message.

  3. Rule-based model ↗

    RuleBasedModel in llm/rule_based.py runs next_message(): plain Python rules, no network. CI and the unit tests use it.

  4. Live model ↗

    ChatOpenAI from langchain_openai. It reads the key from OPENAI_API_KEY or the Compose secret file, OPENAI_MODEL (default gpt-4.1-mini), optional OPENAI_BASE_URL, and AGENT_MAX_TOKENS. This is the one call that leaves your machine. A failed call, such as no credits, ends the run as model_error.

  5. Tool loop ↗

    build_graph() makes a LangGraph with a model node and a tools node. The loop repeats until the model answers or AGENT_MAX_STEPS (default 8) stops it.

  6. Check the answer ↗

    parse_findings() refuses an answer given before any tool call, and evidence for a tool that did not run. It blocks a next step with a command or a destructive word, and any fix other than the one allowed, using safety/guardrails.py.

  7. Findings ↗

    A dict with fault_found, cause, evidence, next_action, and proposed_fix, shaped by agent/schemas.py. investigate() adds steps, stopped_reason, and trace_path.

3

How does one model step reach the cluster?

Diagram structure
  • agent/graph.py agent
  • Model model
  • ToolNode tools
  • tools/ and clients/ reads
  • kind kind
  • agent → model · question and four tools
  • model → agent · one tool call
  • agent → tools · first call only
  • tools → reads · get_pod_status()
  • reads → kind · kubectl get pods -A
  • kind → reads · JSON
  • reads → tools · result text, secrets hidden
  • tools → agent · ToolMessage
  • agent → model · plus the tool result
  • model → agent · answer JSON
  1. agent/graph.py ↗

    The call_model function in build_graph(). It counts the step, calls the model inside a chat <model> trace span, and keeps only the first tool call. A final answer is then checked inside a validate_answer span.

  2. Model ↗

    Gets the system prompt, your question, and every tool result so far. It replies with one tool to run, or with the final JSON.

  3. ToolNode ↗

    A LangGraph class that runs the tool the model named. It is the only route from the model to the cluster.

  4. tools/ and clients/ ↗

    Four @tool functions in tools/kubernetes.py: get_pod_status, get_events, get_pod_logs, and get_setup. Each calls a read in clients/kubernetes.py, which checks names and runs kubectl. The whole result, errors included, then passes redact_payload(), and each call writes a trace span. get_pod_status takes no namespace: it lists every app namespace, unhealthy pods first, at most 100.

  5. kind ↗

    run() in clients/kubectl.py builds kubectl --kubeconfig <file> ... as a list, with no shell and a 30 second limit. In Docker the login is the agent's ServiceAccount token. Kubernetes lets it list pods everywhere, read only in the three app namespaces, and patch only not-ready-app.

4

What does your yes change?

Diagram structure
  • You you
  • cli.py cli
  • agent/remediation.py agent
  • Proposal file file
  • clients/kubernetes.py client
  • kind kind
  • cli → agent · save_proposal(findings)
  • agent → file · write change, status pending
  • you → cli · approve id
  • cli → agent · approve(id)
  • agent → file · read it, must be pending
  • agent → client · patch_readiness_port()
  • client → kind · read the live port
  • client → kind · patch port 8081 to 8080
  • agent → file · mark applied
  • agent → client · pod status and setup
  • client → kind · kubectl get
  • agent → cli · resolved and port
  • cli → you · JSON report
  1. You ↗

    Run k8s-troubleshooter approve <id> with the id from the answer. The agent never applies a change by itself.

  2. cli.py ↗

    Calls approve() and prints its report.

  3. agent/remediation.py ↗

    approve() checks the id has 32 hex characters, the status is pending, and the fix still passes accepted_fix(). After the patch it sets the status to applied, so a second yes is refused.

  4. Proposal file ↗

    traces/proposals/<id>.json, written by save_proposal(). It holds the exact change you approve.

  5. clients/kubernetes.py ↗

    patch_readiness_port() reads the live setup again. It refuses unless the live port equals the saved from_port, and to_port is a port the container listens on.

  6. kind ↗

    One kubectl patch changes that one port. Kubernetes allows it only on not-ready-app in not-ready-app. Then approve() polls pods and setup for up to AGENT_APPROVE_WAIT seconds, 120 by default.

Where do I extend it?

To addChange
A Slack bot or web doorA new file that calls investigate(question) from agent/graph.py and approve(id) from agent/remediation.py
A fifth toolA read in clients/kubernetes.py, a @tool function and a name in TOOL_NAMES in tools/kubernetes.py, a line in SYSTEM_PROMPT, and the matching Kubernetes permission in rbac.yaml
Another model providerOne branch in build_model() in llm/provider.py, plus its LangChain package
Another failureA folder in scenarios/, its namespace in rbac.yaml, and a case in evals/scenarios.py. The rule-based model also needs a rule in _conclude()
